# s007 Semantic Channel Discovery

## Parent Channels

### 1. P1 (7:1-25) - Measured Formation and Standing
- Semantic invariant: A made being receives form, position, and consequence through acts of estimation.
- Surface relation: direct; 7:8-12 joins weighing, creation, form, fire, and clay.
- Surprising reach: The creation root reaches back to pre-cut estimation, making bodily formation and moral weighing two operations of calibrated assignment.

#### Subchannel A. Form Estimated Before It Is Made
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A form is first proportioned, then brought into being, imaged, and given a material constitution.
- Active motifs: pre-action estimation (`quranic:root_000434:B001/m01`); bringing creation into being (`quranic:root_000434:B002/m01`); imaged bodily form (`quranic:root_000891:B003/m01`); mixed clay material (`quranic:root_000963:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:11 `خَلَقْنَاكُمْ` and `صَوَّرْنَاكُمْ`; 7:12 `خَلَقْتَنِي` and `طِينٍ`
- Synthesis: Creation is not merely emergence. Its lexical field supplies an estimating operation before the finished form, while imaging and clay supply configuration and material. The result is a workshop-like scene in which constitution and proportion precede assigned standing.

#### Subchannel B. Standing Made Heavy or Light
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A balance assigns consequence by weight, with heaviness, lightness, rank, and loss as its outcomes.
- Active motifs: estimating by weight (`quranic:root_001645:B001/m01`); scales of justice (`quranic:root_001645:B002/m01`); weighted rank (`quranic:root_001645:B007/m01`); heaviness against lightness (`quranic:root_000202:B001/m01`); lightened load (`quranic:root_000427:B001/m01`); general diminution (`quranic:root_000409:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:8 `الْوَزْنُ`, `ثَقُلَتْ`, and `مَوَازِينُهُ`; 7:9 `خَفَّتْ`, `مَوَازِينُهُ`, and `خَسِرُوا`
- Synthesis: The balance does more than count deeds: it materializes standing as load and rank. A heavy measure establishes consequential substance, while lightness becomes diminished standing and loss.

### 2. P1 (7:1-25) - From Enclosure to Exposed Ground
- Semantic invariant: Crossing a protected boundary lowers status, exposes the body, and requires a new covering and place of settlement.
- Surface relation: direct; 7:13 and 7:18-25 move from expulsion and descent to exposure, patching, and earthly settlement.
- Surprising reach: Forgiveness retains the concrete action of protective covering, so the plea after exposure answers the leaf-patching scene at another level.

#### Subchannel A. Lowered Placement
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Expulsion becomes a descent from rank, attachment to the ground, and temporary stabilization there.
- Active motifs: descent from height (`quranic:root_001575:B001/m01`); abasement from rank (`quranic:root_001575:B002/m01`); passage outside a prior state (`quranic:root_000400:B001/m01`); clinging heavily to earth (`quranic:root_000025:B006/m01`); fixed settlement (`quranic:root_001215:B003/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:13 `فَاهْبِطْ` and `فَاخْرُجْ`; 7:18 `اخْرُجْ`; 7:24 `اهْبِطُوا`, `الْأَرْضِ`, and `مُسْتَقَرٌّ`; 7:25 `تُخْرَجُونَ`
- Synthesis: The motion is simultaneously spatial and positional. Descent removes elevated standing, exit crosses the enclosure, and the ground becomes a fixed but temporary station for life and death.

#### Subchannel B. Concealment Breached and Patched
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Hidden suggestion induces deception; concealment fails; exposed bodies are patched with overlapping leaves; protective covering is sought again.
- Active motifs: hidden inner speech (`quranic:root_001651:B001/m01`); deception by unstable glitter (`quranic:root_001078:B008/m01`); emergence from concealment (`quranic:root_000097:B001/m01`); hiding behind what is shown (`quranic:root_001642:B005/m01`); overlapping material for cover (`quranic:root_000415:B001/m01`); thin leaves or sheets (`quranic:root_001641:B001/m01`); covering that protects (`quranic:root_001096:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:20 `فَوَسْوَسَ`, `لِيُبْدِيَ`, and `وُورِيَ`; 7:22 `بِغُرُورٍ`, `بَدَتْ`, `يَخْصِفَانِ`, and `وَرَقِ`; 7:23 `تَغْفِرْ`
- Synthesis: A concealed mental intrusion produces bodily disclosure. The response is materially exact: flat leaves are layered into a provisional cover. The later request for forgiveness extends the same operation from exposed skin to exposed fault.

### 3. P2 (7:26-39) - Protective Layers and Their Removal
- Semantic invariant: Covering is a layered defense whose value becomes visible when it is stripped away or contrasted with an exposed interior.
- Surface relation: direct; 7:26-27 names clothing, plumage, concealment, and stripping, while 7:33 distinguishes outer and inner.
- Surprising reach: Plumage and armor turn ordinary clothing into both display and fortification.

#### Subchannel A. Clothing as Plumage and Armor
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: The body receives a covering that conceals, adorns like plumage, and can function as defensive equipment.
- Active motifs: bodily covering (`quranic:root_001341:B001/m01`); armor-like protection (`quranic:root_001341:B002/m01`); bird plumage (`quranic:root_000617:B001/m01`); fine dress and ornament (`quranic:root_000617:B002/m01`); concealment behind a surface (`quranic:root_001642:B005/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:26 `لِبَاسًا`, `يُوَارِي`, `رِيشًا`, and `لِبَاسُ`; 7:27 `لِبَاسَهُمَا`
- Synthesis: The garment combines three functions: it hides vulnerability, marks flourishing like feathers, and supplies a defensive layer. The clothing image therefore holds modesty, beauty, and protection in one coherent material object.

#### Subchannel B. Stripping Exposes the Inside
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A covering is pulled from its place, making visible what had been interior or hidden beneath an outer face.
- Active motifs: extraction from a fixed place (`quranic:root_001489:B001/m01`); inner side of a thing (`quranic:root_000128:B001/m01`); garment lining (`quranic:root_000128:B003/m01`); outward emergence (`quranic:root_000970:B001/m01`); back or outer face (`quranic:root_000970:B002/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:27 `يَنْزِعُ`, `لِبَاسَهُمَا`, and `لِيُرِيَهُمَا`; 7:33 `ظَهَرَ` and `بَطَنَ`
- Synthesis: Stripping is an extraction rather than a passive absence. The later outer/inner contrast supplies the geometry of that exposure: an exterior layer can be removed, but concealed states also have an interior face that must be judged.

### 4. P2 (7:26-39) - Apportioned Intake and Experienced Outcome
- Semantic invariant: What is taken into the body is bounded by measure, assigned share, and the consequence eventually tasted.
- Surface relation: direct; 7:31-32 regulates eating, drinking, and provision, while 7:37-39 assigns shares and makes consequence something tasted.
- Surprising reach: The same intake vocabulary links nourishment to allotted record and punishment, turning outcome into embodied consumption.

#### Subchannel A. Eating and Drinking Within a Limit
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: Food and drink are available as nourishment, but consumption is constrained against crossing the proper measure.
- Active motifs: taking food (`quranic:root_000043:B001/m01`); taking liquid (`quranic:root_000783:B001/m01`); crossing the limit (`quranic:root_000699:B001/m01`); sustaining provision (`quranic:root_000560:B002/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:31 `كُلُوا`, `اشْرَبُوا`, and `تُسْرِفُوا`; 7:32 `الرِّزْقِ`
- Synthesis: Permission and restraint belong to one consumption scene. Nourishment is not rejected; excess is the operation that disorders it by carrying intake beyond its fitting boundary.

#### Subchannel B. The Assigned Share Becomes a Taste
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A designated portion arrives from a written allotment and is finally experienced as an earned taste.
- Active motifs: allotted edible share (`quranic:root_000043:B003/m01`); known water share (`quranic:root_000783:B002/m01`); apportioned provision (`quranic:root_000560:B001/m01`); an assigned portion (`quranic:root_001507:B005/m01`); experienced ordeal (`quranic:root_000526:B002/m01`); acquired outcome (`quranic:root_001296:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:31 `كُلُوا` and `اشْرَبُوا`; 7:32 `الرِّزْقِ`; 7:37 `نَصِيبُهُمْ`; 7:39 `فَذُوقُوا` and `تَكْسِبُونَ`
- Synthesis: Portion, provision, earning, and taste form a complete allocation circuit. What reaches each party is not abstract: the assigned outcome passes into direct experience as something consumed.

### 5. P2 (7:26-39) - Ordered Terms and Generational Entry
- Semantic invariant: Communities and outcomes are placed in an order that cannot be advanced, delayed, or escaped by blaming an adjacent generation.
- Surface relation: direct; 7:34 fixes each community's term, and 7:38-39 stages successive entry and dispute between earlier and later groups.
- Surprising reach: The verb of catching up makes collective arrival resemble a queue whose members converge only after entering in sequence.

#### Subchannel A. A Term That Cannot Shift
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: A fixed endpoint arrives without allowing movement backward or forward in the schedule.
- Active motifs: appointed temporal limit (`quranic:root_000016:B001/m01`); postponement to a later time (`quranic:root_000019:B002/m01`); advance before another (`quranic:root_001207:B004/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:34 `أَجَلٌ`, `أَجَلُهُمْ`, `يَسْتَأْخِرُونَ`, and `يَسْتَقْدِمُونَ`
- Synthesis: The term behaves as a non-negotiable slot. Neither postponement nor advancement can alter its arrival, making temporal placement itself part of judgment.

#### Subchannel B. Earlier and Later Parties Catch Up
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Successive communities enter, converge, distinguish first from last, and attempt to transfer a doubled outcome.
- Active motifs: later position (`quranic:root_000019:B001/m01`); first position and precedence (`quranic:root_000067:B001/m01`); catching up and successive convergence (`quranic:root_000471:B001/m01`); increase by a matching multiple (`quranic:root_000909:B002/m01`); ordeal made experiential (`quranic:root_000526:B002/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:38 `دَخَلَتْ`, `ادَّارَكُوا`, `أُخْرَاهُمْ`, `لِأُولَاهُمْ`, and `ضِعْفًا`; 7:39 `أُولَاهُمْ`, `لِأُخْرَاهُمْ`, and `فَذُوقُوا`
- Synthesis: The sequence preserves relational order even after all parties converge. Earlier and later groups remain distinguishable, but neither can displace its share by assigning causation wholly to the other.

### 6. P3 (7:40-58) - Controlled Passage and Recognized Position
- Semantic invariant: Entry depends on fitting a constrained opening, while position at a boundary enables recognition of those on either side.
- Surface relation: direct; 7:40 compresses passage into the camel-and-needle image, and 7:46-48 places recognizable figures on a barrier and its heights.
- Surprising reach: The eyebrow sense of the barrier root turns the elevated boundary into an organ-like sightline.

#### Subchannel A. The Impossible Aperture
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A large body confronts a minute opening associated with thread and sewing; entry fails because object and aperture cannot fit.
- Active motifs: opening a closed entrance (`quranic:root_001124:B001/m01`); narrow perforation (`quranic:root_000743:B001/m01`); full-grown camel (`quranic:root_000260:B001/m01`); needle and sewing tool (`quranic:root_000453:B006/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:40 `تُفَتَّحُ`, `الْجَمَلُ`, `سَمِّ`, and `الْخِيَاطِ`
- Synthesis: The image is a precise fit test. A gate remains closed because a camel cannot be reduced to the scale of the perforation through which thread normally passes.

#### Subchannel B. Boundary as Sightline and Marking Station
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A separating screen rises into a lookout from which persons are distinguished by visible marks.
- Active motifs: separating screen (`quranic:root_000294:B002/m01`); eyebrow-like visual barrier (`quranic:root_000294:B005/m01`); raised ridge or wall (`quranic:root_001002:B002/m01`); recognition by a sign (`quranic:root_001002:B003/m01`); physical sight (`quranic:root_000121:B001/m01`); directed observation (`quranic:root_001520:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:46 `حِجَابٌ`, `الْأَعْرَافِ`, and `يَعْرِفُونَ`; 7:47 `أَبْصَارُهُمْ`; 7:48 `الْأَعْرَافِ` and `يَعْرِفُونَهُمْ`; 7:53 `يَنْظُرُونَ`
- Synthesis: The barrier does not only prevent crossing. Its raised edge organizes perception: like a brow above the eye, it becomes a station from which marks can be read and positions on both sides distinguished.

### 7. P3 (7:40-58) - Hydraulic Renewal and Productive Sorting
- Semantic invariant: Water is transported, released, and received by land whose condition determines what can emerge.
- Surface relation: direct; 7:50 and 7:57-58 link water, cloud movement, dead land, fruit, good soil, and poor yield.
- Surprising reach: The water root includes abundance within wells and fruit, making revival a transfer of internal moisture as well as external rain.

#### Subchannel A. Cloud Load Delivered as Water
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A dragged cloud bears a heavy load, is sent toward dead land, and releases abundant water.
- Active motifs: cloud drawn through the air (`quranic:root_000680:B002/m01`); heavy load (`quranic:root_000202:B001/m01`); known water substance (`quranic:root_001458:B001/m01`); water appearing in abundance (`quranic:root_001458:B002/m01`); dispatch and release (`quranic:root_000563:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:50 `الْمَاءَ`; 7:57 `يُرْسِلُ`, `سَحَابًا`, `ثِقَالًا`, and `الْمَاءَ`
- Synthesis: The cloud behaves as a transported reservoir. Its heaviness signals stored contents, dispatch supplies direction, and release transfers that load into a landscape unable to revive itself.

#### Subchannel B. Land Sorts Water into Growth or Scarcity
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Received water produces fruit and vegetation according to the receiving land's quality.
- Active motifs: bounded tract of land (`quranic:root_000148:B001/m01`); ripe fruit (`quranic:root_000205:B001/m01`); plants emerging from soil (`quranic:root_001465:B001/m01`); wholesome quality (`quranic:root_000961:B001/m01`); foul or defective quality (`quranic:root_000386:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:57 `بَلَدٍ`, `الثَّمَرَاتِ`; 7:58 `الْبَلَدُ`, `الطَّيِّبُ`, `نَبَاتُهُ`, and `خَبُثَ`
- Synthesis: Water is common input, but land is an active receiving medium. Good ground converts the input into abundant emergence; defective ground constrains the same process to sparse output.

### 8. P4 (7:59-72) - Delivered Counsel and Trust
- Semantic invariant: A message reaches its audience through a carrier whose counsel must be both intelligible and free of hidden corruption.
- Surface relation: direct; 7:59-70 repeatedly joins messenger, delivery, counsel, reminder, and trust.
- Surprising reach: Counsel also denotes sewing a tear, recasting the messenger's work as repair of a damaged communal fabric.

#### Subchannel A. A Message Carried to Its Limit
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A carrier bears speech and delivers it until it reaches the intended audience in an intelligible form.
- Active motifs: messenger and carried message (`quranic:root_000563:B002/m01`); bringing a message through (`quranic:root_000151:B002/m01`); speech that reaches its intended meaning (`quranic:root_000151:B004/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:59 `أَرْسَلْنَا`; 7:61 `رَسُولٌ`; 7:62 `أُبَلِّغُكُمْ` and `رِسَالَاتِ`; 7:67 `رَسُولٌ`; 7:68 `أُبَلِّغُكُمْ` and `رِسَالَاتِ`
- Synthesis: Delivery requires both transport and arrival in understanding. The carrier does not merely possess a message; the act is complete only when speech reaches its addressee with enough clarity to perform its warning.

#### Subchannel B. Counsel as Clean Repair
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A trusted counselor removes deceit from advice and repairs a communal tear as a sewer closes a rupture.
- Active motifs: beneficial counsel (`quranic:root_001509:B001/m01`); purity from deceit (`quranic:root_001509:B002/m01`); stitching a tear closed (`quranic:root_001509:B003/m01`); secure trust (`quranic:root_000054:B001/m01`); spoken reminder (`quranic:root_000516:B004/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:62 `أَنْصَحُ`; 7:63 `ذِكْرٌ`; 7:68 `نَاصِحٌ` and `أَمِينٌ`; 7:69 `ذِكْرٌ`
- Synthesis: Integrity is represented as material repair. Counsel is clean because it contains no hidden fraud, and it is reparative because it draws separated edges back together under a trusted hand.

### 9. P4 (7:59-72) - Succession or Erasure
- Semantic invariant: A former community can be followed by a successor, or its remaining line can be cut so that no trace continues.
- Surface relation: direct; 7:69 names succession after another people, while 7:72 names the cutting of the deniers' last remnant.
- Surprising reach: Alternating succession carries the image of one wave or shift replacing another, in sharp contrast to a severed rear with no next member.

#### Subchannel A. A Successor Takes the Former Place
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: One group arrives after another and occupies the position left behind.
- Active motifs: successor standing in another's place (`quranic:root_000433:B001/m01`); alternating replacement (`quranic:root_000433:B006/m01`); temporal position after a predecessor (`quranic:root_000131:B002/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:69 `خُلَفَاءَ` and `مِنْ بَعْدِ`
- Synthesis: Succession is spatial as well as temporal. The later group inherits a vacated position and becomes the next bearer of strength, memory, and obligation.

#### Subchannel B. The Rear Trace Is Cut
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: The final segment of a group is severed, ending continuation and erasing the line behind it.
- Active motifs: cutting the last remnant and its trace (`quranic:root_000458:B004/m01`); severance and ending (`quranic:root_001240:B005/m01`); broken connection (`quranic:root_001240:B007/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:72 `وَقَطَعْنَا` and `دَابِرَ`
- Synthesis: Unlike succession, excision leaves no replacement path. Cutting reaches the rear of the group and removes the residual trace from which continuity might have resumed.

### 10. P5 (7:73-102) - Settlement Built and Shaken
- Semantic invariant: A community stabilizes itself by shaping terrain into dwellings, but the same settled form can be immobilized and enclosed by disaster.
- Surface relation: direct; 7:74 describes prepared settlement and carved houses, while 7:78 and 7:91 repeat the quake, house, and prostrate body scene.
- Surprising reach: The dwelling root also names a grave, sharpening the conversion of inhabited houses into places occupied by motionless bodies.

#### Subchannel A. Terrain Converted into Habitation
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Plain and mountain are selected, enclosed, cut, and prepared as durable dwelling space.
- Active motifs: prepared place of settlement (`quranic:root_000161:B001/m01`); smooth plain (`quranic:root_000753:B001/m01`); enclosed palace (`quranic:root_001231:B005/m01`); cutting hard material with a tool (`quranic:root_001478:B001/m01`); raised solid mountain (`quranic:root_000217:B001/m01`); sheltering house (`quranic:root_000166:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:74 `بَوَّأَكُمْ`, `سُهُولِهَا`, `قُصُورًا`, `تَنْحِتُونَ`, `الْجِبَالَ`, and `بُيُوتًا`
- Synthesis: Settlement is an engineered transformation of terrain. Open plain becomes enclosed architecture, and mountain mass is cut into interior shelter, producing a deliberately stabilized civic habitat.

#### Subchannel B. Houses Become Sites of Immobilization
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A severe shaking overtakes the settlement; bodies adhere to the ground inside their homes as an encircling defeat closes over them.
- Active motifs: violent oscillation (`quranic:root_000545:B001/m01`); resident fixed in a dwelling (`quranic:root_000499:B007/m01`); enclosing calamity or defeat (`quranic:root_000499:B004/m01`); body fixed to the ground (`quranic:root_000222:B001/m01`); bodily remains (`quranic:root_000222:B003/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:78 and 7:91 `الرَّجْفَةُ`, `دَارِهِمْ`, and `جَاثِمِينَ`
- Synthesis: Built stability is reversed into terminal stillness. The quake moves the settlement violently, but its outcome is bodies that cannot move at all, fixed within the very domestic enclosure meant to secure life.

### 11. P5 (7:73-102) - Regulated Access to Shared Resources
- Semantic invariant: Common life depends on protected access to grazing land, fair exchange, and unobstructed routes.
- Surface relation: direct; 7:73-77 regulates the camel's grazing, 7:85 regulates measure, and 7:86 prohibits ambush and obstruction on the road.
- Surprising reach: The hamstringing root also reaches to landed estate, so violence against the camel pressures the wider economy of land, stock, and household property.

#### Subchannel A. Grazing Animal and Landed Estate
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A designated camel is released into common land to feed, then disabled by cutting its legs.
- Active motifs: the she-camel and its form (`quranic:root_001567:B002/m01`); crop or pasture yield (`quranic:root_000043:B002/m01`); fertile growing earth (`quranic:root_000025:B002/m01`); cutting an animal's legs (`quranic:root_001035:B002/m01`); estate, land, and household property (`quranic:root_001035:B016/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:73 `نَاقَةُ`, `تَأْكُلْ`, and `أَرْضِ`; 7:77 `فَعَقَرُوا` and `النَّاقَةَ`
- Synthesis: The camel is a living claimant on shared pasture. Disabling it is therefore not only bodily violence; the estate sense of the same root expands the act into an assault on the ordered relation among animal, land, and communal property.

#### Subchannel B. Exchange Calibrated Without Deficit
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Food is measured, value is weighed, completion is required, and no party's due may be reduced.
- Active motifs: measuring food (`quranic:root_001335:B001/m01`); estimating by a balance (`quranic:root_001645:B001/m01`); just scales (`quranic:root_001645:B002/m01`); diminution of another's right (`quranic:root_000087:B001/m01`); completion without deficit (`quranic:root_001669:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:85 `فَأَوْفُوا`, `الْكَيْلَ`, `الْمِيزَانَ`, and `تَبْخَسُوا`
- Synthesis: Fair exchange is a sequence of calibrated acts. The seller fills, measures, and weighs; the social outcome is just only when the recipient's portion emerges whole.

#### Subchannel C. The Road Kept Open
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Watchers sit at routes, threaten travelers, block a path, and seek to bend its direction.
- Active motifs: sitting in ambush (`quranic:root_001244:B005/m01`); straight road (`quranic:root_000858:B001/m01`); traveled route (`quranic:root_000672:B001/m01`); road users (`quranic:root_000672:B002/m01`); active obstruction (`quranic:root_000848:B001/m01`); bending a meaning away from straightness (`quranic:root_001057:B002/m01`); threatening approach (`quranic:root_001662:B002/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:86 `تَقْعُدُوا`, `صِرَاطٍ`, `تُوعِدُونَ`, `تَصُدُّونَ`, `سَبِيلِ`, and `عِوَجًا`
- Synthesis: Route control is a social technology of exclusion. A stationary watcher converts a public path into a checkpoint, and the desired bend is both a deviation in travel and a distortion in guidance.

### 12. P5 (7:73-102) - Alternating Conditions and Sudden Closure
- Semantic invariant: Conditions can be exchanged and enlarged without warning, so apparent security never controls the timing of closure.
- Surface relation: direct; 7:94-95 replaces hardship with ease, then 7:95-98 stages sudden seizure during sleep or play.
- Surprising reach: Growth after neglect makes prosperity itself part of the test: unattended increase can conceal rather than cancel exposure.

#### Subchannel A. Hardship Replaced by Expanding Ease
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: One condition is installed in place of another; hardship yields to ease and the population grows until it reads alternation as ordinary inheritance.
- Active motifs: substitution of one thing for another (`quranic:root_000095:B001/m01`); change of condition (`quranic:root_000095:B002/m01`); constricted livelihood (`quranic:root_000079:B002/m01`); hidden ease and prosperity (`quranic:root_000697:B010/m01`); increase after being left alone (`quranic:root_001032:B007/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:94 `بِالْبَأْسَاءِ`; 7:95 `بَدَّلْنَا`, `الضَّرَّاءُ`, `السَّرَّاءُ`, and `عَفَوْا`
- Synthesis: Alternation is an active replacement mechanism. Scarcity is removed, prosperity occupies its place, and unchecked increase encourages the mistaken inference that both states are merely inherited cycles without accountability.

#### Subchannel B. Closure Arrives Off Schedule
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Sudden seizure interrupts people at their least guarded temporal positions: asleep at night or playing in broad morning.
- Active motifs: unanticipated surprise (`quranic:root_000135:B001/m01`); action occurring by night (`quranic:root_000166:B004/m01`); sleep (`quranic:root_001568:B001/m01`); elevated morning time (`quranic:root_000904:B001/m01`); purposeless play (`quranic:root_001358:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:95 `بَغْتَةً`; 7:97 `بَيَاتًا` and `نَائِمُونَ`; 7:98 `ضُحًى` and `يَلْعَبُونَ`
- Synthesis: Night and morning cover opposite routines, yet neither provides temporal immunity. Surprise breaks the imagined schedule by arriving during both unconscious rest and careless activity.

### 13. P6 (7:103-129) - Staged Public Contest
- Semantic invariant: Authority is contested through recruitment, spectacle, competing signs, and a public reversal of the expected victor.
- Surface relation: direct; 7:109-120 moves from gathering skilled performers and bargaining over reward to visual enchantment, swallowing, defeat, and prostration.
- Surprising reach: The contest's vocabulary spans court patronage, induced fear, rapid ingestion, and bodily inversion, making belief change the final stage action.

#### Subchannel A. Performers Recruited for Reward and Rank
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Specialists are gathered from cities, bargain for payment, and seek proximity to the ruling court through victory.
- Active motifs: gathering and driving a group to one destination (`quranic:root_000324:B001/m01`); fortified city as recruitment field (`quranic:root_001408:B001/m01`); contracted wage (`quranic:root_000015:B001/m01`); court favorite near the ruler (`quranic:root_001212:B004/m01`); coercive victory (`quranic:root_001098:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:111 `الْمَدَائِنِ` and `حَاشِرِينَ`; 7:113 `لَأَجْرًا` and `الْغَالِبِينَ`; 7:114 `الْمُقَرَّبِينَ`
- Synthesis: The contest is institutionally staged. Urban recruitment supplies performers, wage supplies incentive, and nearness to power supplies the promised promotion if their spectacle prevails.

#### Subchannel B. Sight Captured, Then the Display Swallowed
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Visual deception seizes the audience's eyes and induces fear until a staff becomes a great serpent and rapidly ingests the fabricated display.
- Active motifs: deceptive diversion (`quranic:root_000682:B002/m01`); direct eye-witnessing (`quranic:root_001069:B002/m01`); harmful capture of the eye (`quranic:root_001069:B004/m01`); induced fear (`quranic:root_000604:B002/m01`); hand-held staff (`quranic:root_005713:B001/m01`); great extended serpent (`quranic:root_000199:B002/m01`); rapid taking and swallowing (`quranic:root_001370:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:107 `عَصَاهُ` and `ثُعْبَانٌ`; 7:116 `سَحَرُوا`, `أَعْيُنَ`, and `اسْتَرْهَبُوهُمْ`; 7:117 `عَصَاكَ` and `تَلْقَفُ`
- Synthesis: The first display controls perception rather than substance. The counter-sign changes the material relation: what had occupied sight as fabricated magnitude is treated as ingestible matter and removed by a single rapid action.

#### Subchannel C. Defeat Becomes Bodily Inversion
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: The manufactured act falls void, the expected winners are overturned, and the performers themselves drop into submission.
- Active motifs: audible impact of falling (`quranic:root_001675:B004/m01`); reversal from one face to another (`quranic:root_001248:B004/m01`); defeat by overpowering force (`quranic:root_001098:B001/m01`); prostrating submission (`quranic:root_000675:B001/m01`); bowed head and bent posture (`quranic:root_000675:B004/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:118 `فَوَقَعَ`; 7:119 `فَغُلِبُوا` and `انْقَلَبُوا`; 7:120 `سَاجِدِينَ`
- Synthesis: The reversal is registered on bodies. A promised triumph becomes defeat, standing performers become prostrate witnesses, and the public stage produces the opposite allegiance from the one it was designed to secure.

### 14. P6 (7:103-129) - Competing Uses of the Hand
- Semantic invariant: The hand can bear a sign of authority or become the object and instrument of coercive state power.
- Surface relation: direct; 7:107-108 and 7:117 place staff and white hand in the sign sequence, while 7:124-127 threatens cutting, crucifixion, and selective killing.
- Surprising reach: The hand's lexical range from bodily member to sovereign power lets the same image mediate demonstrated authority and mutilating authority.

#### Subchannel A. Hand, Staff, and Visible Sign
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A hand controls a staff, then emerges white as a visible sign before witnesses.
- Active motifs: bodily hand (`quranic:root_001693:B001/m01`); hand as effective authority (`quranic:root_001693:B005/m01`); visible whiteness (`quranic:root_000168:B001/m01`); held staff (`quranic:root_005713:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:107 `عَصَاهُ`; 7:108 `يَدَهُ` and `بَيْضَاءُ`; 7:117 `عَصَاكَ`
- Synthesis: Authority is displayed through controlled bodily instruments. The staff acts outwardly, while the hand itself becomes visible evidence, joining tool, limb, and sign in one demonstrative sequence.

#### Subchannel B. Sovereignty Written onto Bodies
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Ruling power answers allegiance by cutting opposite limbs, suspending bodies, and reviving a prior policy of selective killing.
- Active motifs: bodily severance (`quranic:root_001240:B001/m01`); suspension for execution (`quranic:root_000875:B005/m01`); killing and removal of life (`quranic:root_001200:B001/m01`); domination from above (`quranic:root_001188:B003/m01`); preserving selected lives (`quranic:root_000383:B006/m01`); sons and lineage (`quranic:root_000156:B007/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:124 `لَأُقَطِّعَنَّ`, `أَيْدِيَكُمْ`, `أَرْجُلَكُمْ`, and `لَأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ`; 7:127 `يُقَتِّلَ`, `أَبْنَاءَهُمْ`, `يَسْتَحْيِي`, and `فَوْقَهُمْ`
- Synthesis: Political control is imposed directly on limbs and reproduction. Cutting marks bodies, crucifixion displays them, and selective killing attempts to govern the community's future lineage.

### 15. P7 (7:130-147) - Ecological Pressure and Watery Release
- Semantic invariant: Land, crop, animal, and water become coordinated pressure points whose release culminates in passage for one group and submersion for another.
- Surface relation: direct; 7:130-136 moves through crop shortage, pests, blood, flood, removal, and drowning, with 7:138 completing the sea passage.
- Surprising reach: Locust imagery explicitly strips land of its vegetal cover, making plague a progressive unmaking of the productive surface.

#### Subchannel A. Productive Surface Stripped
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Fruit diminishes, consuming swarms and vermin invade, frogs occupy the environment, and blood corrupts the water system.
- Active motifs: loss of part or yield (`quranic:root_001542:B001/m01`); mature fruit (`quranic:root_000205:B001/m01`); locust that strips vegetation (`quranic:root_000234:B004/m01`); lice and tiny vermin (`quranic:root_001259:B001/m01`); frogs (`quranic:root_000912:B001/m01`); blood substance (`quranic:root_000490:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:130 `نَقْصٍ` and `الثَّمَرَاتِ`; 7:133 `الْجَرَادَ`, `الْقُمَّلَ`, `الضَّفَادِعَ`, and `الدَّمَ`
- Synthesis: The pressure sequence dismantles subsistence at multiple scales. Yield falls, vegetation is eaten away, small organisms saturate daily space, and the water medium itself becomes blood.

#### Subchannel B. Encompassing Water Sorts Passage from Drowning
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: An enclosing flood is removed and followed by a sea crossing whose pursuing party is submerged.
- Active motifs: all-encompassing flood (`quranic:root_000957:B002/m01`); broad abundant water (`quranic:root_000086:B001/m01`); sinking to death (`quranic:root_001080:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:133 `الطُّوفَانَ`; 7:136 `فَأَغْرَقْنَاهُمْ`; 7:138 `الْبَحْرَ`
- Synthesis: Water changes role without losing material continuity. It first surrounds as plague, then opens as a route, and finally closes over the pursuing force as a terminal boundary.

### 16. P7 (7:130-147) - Promise Under Repeated Reversal
- Semantic invariant: Relief is negotiated through a maintained promise, but removal of pressure exposes whether the bond remains tied.
- Surface relation: direct; 7:134-135 couples pledged relief, a fixed endpoint, removal, and immediate breach.
- Surprising reach: Breach is pictured as unraveling tightly made rope or woven fabric, making covenant failure a material undoing.

#### Subchannel A. Relief Conditioned by a Maintained Bond
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A party asks for removal of affliction under a promise to change course before an appointed limit.
- Active motifs: repeated maintenance and care (`quranic:root_001055:B001/m01`); protected covenant (`quranic:root_001055:B003/m01`); lifting a covering affliction (`quranic:root_001302:B001/m01`); fixed temporal endpoint (`quranic:root_000016:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:134 `عَهِدَ`, `لَئِنْ كَشَفْتَ`; 7:135 `كَشَفْنَا` and `أَجَلٍ`
- Synthesis: Relief is not isolated from obligation. The request invokes a maintained bond, and removal opens a probationary interval extending only to a fixed term.

#### Subchannel B. The Tightened Bond Unravels
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Once pressure is removed, a confirmed bond is pulled apart like spun material undone after tightening.
- Active motifs: unraveling woven or twisted material (`quranic:root_001547:B001/m01`); breaking a confirmed covenant (`quranic:root_001547:B002/m01`); exposure of a hidden defect (`quranic:root_001302:B002/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:135 `كَشَفْنَا` and `يَنْكُثُونَ`
- Synthesis: Breach is not mere nonperformance. It reverses construction: a bond previously tightened into strength is picked apart, and relief reveals the defect that pressure had temporarily concealed.

### 17. P7 (7:130-147) - Large Forms Unmade
- Semantic invariant: Human works and natural mass appear durable until a superior event removes their structural integrity.
- Surface relation: direct; 7:137 destroys manufactured and trellised works, while 7:143 levels the mountain and overwhelms human consciousness.
- Surprising reach: Reservoirs and fortified buildings sit inside the craft vocabulary, so the destroyed works include the infrastructure by which a civilization stores and governs resources.

#### Subchannel A. Manufactured Works and Trellises Destroyed
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Skilled production raises buildings, reservoirs, and supported growth; destruction then removes the whole made order.
- Active motifs: deliberate making (`quranic:root_000885:B001/m01`); reservoirs and fortified structures (`quranic:root_000885:B006/m01`); trellised cultivation (`quranic:root_001000:B003/m01`); exterminating destruction (`quranic:root_000487:B002/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:137 `يَصْنَعُ`, `يَعْرِشُونَ`, and `دَمَّرْنَا`
- Synthesis: The scene is not generic ruin. It targets an integrated made environment: craft, water infrastructure, buildings, and cultivated supports are all exposed as contingent forms.

#### Subchannel B. Mountain Mass and Human Awareness Collapse
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A solid mountain is pulverized and flattened; the observer loses consciousness and later returns to awareness.
- Active motifs: solid elevated mountain (`quranic:root_000217:B001/m01`); demolition to ground level (`quranic:root_000482:B001/m01`); flattened low mass (`quranic:root_000482:B002/m01`); stunned loss of consciousness (`quranic:root_000864:B003/m01`); recovery of awareness (`quranic:root_001188:B005/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:143 `لِلْجَبَلِ`, `دَكًّا`, `صَعِقًا`, and `أَفَاقَ`
- Synthesis: Structural and perceptual stability fail in parallel. The mountain loses height and coherence, while the witness loses awareness; recovery belongs to the human observer, not to the leveled mass.

### 18. P8 (7:148-158) - Manufactured Body Without Guiding Speech
- Semantic invariant: A fabricated form can possess body and sound while lacking intelligible communication and directional agency.
- Surface relation: direct; 7:148 contrasts an ornament-made calf with its lowing, inability to speak, and inability to guide.
- Surprising reach: The body root includes dried, adhered blood and saturated dye, keeping the calf's apparent solidity close to processed material rather than living agency.

#### Subchannel A. Ornament Assembled into a Body
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Portable adornment is gathered and converted into the coherent form of a calf.
- Active motifs: wearable ornament (`quranic:root_000353:B001/m01`); assembled bodily form (`quranic:root_000245:B001/m01`); calf as bovine offspring (`quranic:root_000987:B002/m01`); dried adhering blood or material (`quranic:root_000245:B002/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:148 `حُلِيِّهِمْ`, `عِجْلًا`, and `جَسَدًا`
- Synthesis: The calf is a successful artifact at the level of visible form. Ornament is reorganized into a bounded body, yet the lexical material remains processed and adherent rather than self-generating life.

#### Subchannel B. Sound Without Speech or Direction
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: The body emits an animal lowing but cannot engage in reciprocal speech or lead along a path.
- Active motifs: bovine lowing (`quranic:root_000445:B001/m01`); intelligible reciprocal speech (`quranic:root_001316:B001/m01`); gentle direction to a path (`quranic:root_001583:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:148 `خُوَارٌ`, `يُكَلِّمُهُمْ`, and `يَهْدِيهِمْ`
- Synthesis: Audible output is not equivalent to communicative agency. Lowing proves only that the artifact can produce a sound; the missing capacities are intelligible relation and directional guidance.

### 19. P8 (7:148-158) - Anger Handled and Stilled
- Semantic invariant: Anger moves through the body and its objects, then subsides enough for discarded instruction to be recovered.
- Surface relation: direct; 7:150-154 moves from anger, grief, throwing, grabbing, and dragging to stillness and renewed possession of the tablets.
- Surprising reach: Copying preserves an original while transferring its form, allowing recovered tablets to signify continuity after a disruptive emotional episode.

#### Subchannel A. Anger Becomes Grasping and Dragging
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Intense grieving anger is discharged through thrown objects, a seized head, and bodily dragging.
- Active motifs: surging anger directed toward reprisal (`quranic:root_001092:B001/m01`); anger mixed with grief (`quranic:root_000032:B002/m01`); drawing an object by force (`quranic:root_000235:B001/m01`); head and uppermost part (`quranic:root_000529:B001/m01`); taking into one's grasp (`quranic:root_000018:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:150 `غَضْبَانَ`, `أَسِفًا`, `أَلْقَى`, `أَخَذَ`, `بِرَأْسِ`, and `يَجُرُّهُ`
- Synthesis: The affect is kinetic. Anger leaves inward feeling and enters the handling of bodies and objects: tablets are cast down, a head is seized, and a person is pulled into the force of the dispute.

#### Subchannel B. Stillness Permits Recovery
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Once the moving force of anger becomes still, the tablets are taken up and their transmitted content re-enters use.
- Active motifs: stilling what had raged (`quranic:root_000724:B002/m01`); copying while preserving an original (`quranic:root_001495:B002/m01`); broad tablet for writing (`quranic:root_001384:B003/m01`); protective forgiveness (`quranic:root_001096:B002/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:153 `غَفُورٌ`; 7:154 `سَكَتَ`, `أَخَذَ`, and `الْأَلْوَاحَ`; 7:155 `اغْفِرْ`
- Synthesis: Recovery requires a change of state, not denial of the prior rupture. When anger ceases to move, the written object can be retrieved; its copied or transmissible form preserves instruction across the interruption.

### 20. P8 (7:148-158) - Written Obligation and Released Load
- Semantic invariant: Instruction can bind as a written obligation, yet the prophetic work also removes inherited loads and restraints.
- Surface relation: direct; 7:154-157 joins tablets, writing, book, burdens, fetters, and their removal.
- Surprising reach: Writing and binding share concrete operations of joining and fixing, while release is expressed by physically putting a load down.

#### Subchannel A. Instruction Fixed in a Durable Medium
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A tablet bears copied signs whose written form establishes binding judgment.
- Active motifs: written document (`quranic:root_001283:B002/m01`); decree fixed as obligation (`quranic:root_001283:B003/m01`); copied text with original preserved (`quranic:root_001495:B002/m01`); broad writing tablet (`quranic:root_001384:B003/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:154 `الْأَلْوَاحَ`; 7:156 `اكْتُبْ`; 7:157 `مَكْتُوبًا`
- Synthesis: Instruction is stabilized through medium and operation. The tablet supplies a surface, copying preserves transmissibility, and writing fixes the content into an obligation that can outlast its first delivery.

#### Subchannel B. Yoke and Fetter Put Down
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A binding load and iron restraint are removed from those carrying them and placed down.
- Active motifs: captivity by a constraining knot (`quranic:root_000037:B001/m01`); heavy carried obligation (`quranic:root_000037:B004/m01`); iron collar or fetter (`quranic:root_001102:B006/m01`); lowering a load into place (`quranic:root_001657:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:157 `يَضَعُ`, `إِصْرَهُمْ`, and `الْأَغْلَالَ`
- Synthesis: Release is rendered as load handling. Obligation has weight, fetters hold limbs, and liberation occurs when both are taken off the carrier and put down.

### 21. P9 (7:159-171) - Partitioned Commons
- Semantic invariant: A large people is divided into countable groups whose access to water is made distinct and knowable.
- Surface relation: direct; 7:160 divides the people into twelve tribes and assigns twelve springs and recognized drinking places.
- Surprising reach: The cutting root frames tribal division as material segmentation, while watering vocabulary turns each segment into a managed channel and share.

#### Subchannel A. A Whole Cut into Twelve Groups
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A collective is segmented, counted as two plus ten, and maintained as distinct communities.
- Active motifs: separated group or piece (`quranic:root_001240:B002/m01`); division into parts (`quranic:root_001240:B008/m01`); joining one to one as two (`quranic:root_000208:B001/m01`); number ten (`quranic:root_001016:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:160 `وَقَطَّعْنَاهُمُ`, `اثْنَتَيْ`, and `عَشْرَةَ`
- Synthesis: The number is built and embodied in social segmentation. Two and ten compose twelve, while cutting turns arithmetic into organized communal form.

#### Subchannel B. Stone Opened into Known Water Shares
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A staff strikes stone; openings release springs; each group recognizes its own drinking allotment.
- Active motifs: staff as hand-held tool (`quranic:root_005713:B001/m01`); hard stone (`quranic:root_000296:B003/m01`); fissure releasing water (`quranic:root_000084:B001/m01`); running spring (`quranic:root_001069:B006/m01`); irrigation share and channel (`quranic:root_000722:B003/m01`); assigned water portion (`quranic:root_000783:B002/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:160 `بِعَصَاكَ`, `الْحَجَرَ`, `فَانْبَجَسَتْ`, `عَيْنًا`, `مَشْرَبَهُمْ`, and `اسْقُوا`
- Synthesis: The commons is neither undifferentiated nor privately seized. A single stone is opened into multiple flows, and recognition converts those flows into stable, publicly intelligible shares.

### 22. P9 (7:159-171) - Timed Access and Bodily Transformation
- Semantic invariant: Access to a resource is tested by a temporal boundary; repeated circumvention turns a scheduling violation into a transformed social body.
- Surface relation: direct; 7:163-166 links Sabbath timing, visible fish, testing, failed prohibition, and transformation into apes.
- Surprising reach: The Sabbath root combines rest with cutting, making the prohibited interval both cessation of labor and a hard temporal division.

#### Subchannel A. Fish Appear at the Rest Boundary
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Fish become openly available at the water access point on the prohibited day and withdraw on other days.
- Active motifs: day of rest and work cessation (`quranic:root_000665:B003/m01`); cutting and removal (`quranic:root_000665:B002/m01`); fish (`quranic:root_000366:B001/m01`); visible watering access (`quranic:root_000789:B002/m01`); nearness and exposure at the waterline (`quranic:root_000789:B009/m01`); crossing a set limit (`quranic:root_000993:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:163 `السَّبْتِ`, `حِيتَانُهُمْ`, `شُرَّعًا`, `لَا يَسْبِتُونَ`, and `يَفْسُقُونَ`
- Synthesis: The test is engineered through timing and visibility. The resource is most exposed precisely when taking it is forbidden, so the temporal boundary becomes as concrete as the shoreline.

#### Subchannel B. Failed Restraint Ends in a New Form
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A community is tested; warning fails to stop transgression; expulsion and degradation culminate in ape form.
- Active motifs: trial that reveals condition (`quranic:root_000153:B002/m01`); restraining prohibition (`quranic:root_001560:B001/m01`); ape body (`quranic:root_001214:B001/m01`); expulsion with humiliation (`quranic:root_000408:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:163 `نَبْلُوهُمْ`; 7:165 `يَنْهَوْنَ`; 7:166 `نُهُوا`, `قِرَدَةً`, and `خَاسِئِينَ`
- Synthesis: The process moves from verbal restraint to exposed condition and finally bodily outcome. When the boundary no longer governs action, transformation makes the failed moral distinction visible in form.

### 23. P9 (7:159-171) - Held Text Under an Overhead Bond
- Semantic invariant: Inherited instruction must be held firmly while a physically raised mass materializes the force of the covenant.
- Surface relation: direct; 7:169-171 joins inheritance of the book, study, firm adherence, covenant, and the mountain lifted like a canopy.
- Surprising reach: Strength is gathered like the strands of a rope, linking firm textual adherence to the binding force of the overhead covenant.

#### Subchannel A. Inherited Text Studied and Gripped
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A later generation inherits a written document, studies it, and is required to maintain a firm hold on its binding content.
- Active motifs: inherited book or knowledge (`quranic:root_001639:B003/m01`); repeated study until retained (`quranic:root_000470:B002/m01`); holding and preserving (`quranic:root_001424:B001/m01`); confirmed covenant (`quranic:root_001623:B004/m01`); written document (`quranic:root_001283:B002/m01`); binding decree (`quranic:root_001283:B003/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:169 `وَرِثُوا`, `الْكِتَابَ`, `دَرَسُوا`, and `مِيثَاقُ`; 7:170 `يُمَسِّكُونَ` and `بِالْكِتَابِ`
- Synthesis: Transmission is incomplete without handling. Inheritance gives possession, study gives familiarity, and gripping converts the written covenant into maintained practice.

#### Subchannel B. Mountain Lifted as Canopy and Constraint
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A mountain is pulled from its base and held overhead like a covering that may fall.
- Active motifs: lifting and wrenching from the root (`quranic:root_001471:B001/m01`); solid mountain mass (`quranic:root_000217:B001/m01`); overhead canopy (`quranic:root_000966:B003/m01`); strength gathered like rope strands (`quranic:root_001274:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:171 `نَتَقْنَا`, `الْجَبَلَ`, `ظُلَّةٌ`, and `بِقُوَّةٍ`
- Synthesis: The covenant becomes architectural pressure. A mass normally fixed to the earth is uprooted and made into an overhead cover whose possible fall turns instruction into an immediate bodily constraint.

### 24. P10 (7:172-188) - Extracted Lineage and Self-Witness
- Semantic invariant: A distributed lineage is drawn from prior bodies and made present to testify about its own identity.
- Surface relation: direct; 7:172-173 joins sons, backs, descendants, self-witness, fathers, and later generations.
- Surprising reach: Descendant language resonates with scattered minute particles and grains, materializing lineage as multiplicity dispersed from a prior body.

#### Subchannel A. Multiplicity Drawn from Backs
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Sons yield a dispersed multitude from their backs, establishing a relation between predecessor and later offspring.
- Active motifs: filiation and descent (`quranic:root_000156:B007/m01`); bodily back (`quranic:root_000970:B002/m01`); minute particles spreading (`quranic:root_000511:B001/m01`); grains scattered apart (`quranic:root_000511:B002/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:172 `بَنِي`, `ظُهُورِهِمْ`, and `ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ`; 7:173 `ذُرِّيَّةً`
- Synthesis: Lineage is represented as extraction followed by distribution. The back supplies bodily origin, while the particle imagery makes descendants a numerous spread emerging from prior generations.

#### Subchannel B. The Self Made Witness to Itself
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Each self is made present, shown its own relation, and required to bear explicit testimony.
- Active motifs: presence with direct witnessing (`quranic:root_000822:B001/m01`); declaration based on knowledge (`quranic:root_000822:B002/m01`); identifying sign (`quranic:root_000822:B008/m01`); the thing's own identity and essence (`quranic:root_001533:B012/m01`); lapse of attention (`quranic:root_001097:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:172 `أَشْهَدَهُمْ`, `أَنْفُسِهِمْ`, `شَهِدْنَا`, and `غَافِلِينَ`
- Synthesis: Witnessing closes the distance between knower and known. The testified object is the witness's own identity, preventing later inattention from functioning as a substitute account of the relation.

### 25. P10 (7:172-188) - Shedding and Grounded Appetite
- Semantic invariant: Separation from a protective sign is followed by attachment to the lowest surface and a repetitive appetite that no external pressure satisfies.
- Surface relation: direct; 7:175-176 moves from shedding signs to satanic pursuit, earthward attachment, desire, dog, load, release, and panting.
- Surprising reach: Skinning, garment removal, and an animal's shed skin make departure from signs a bodily loss of covering rather than a purely intellectual change.

#### Subchannel A. Signs Shed Like Skin or Clothing
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A person exits received signs as an animal leaves skin or a body removes clothing, allowing pursuit to attach.
- Active motifs: removal of skin or shell (`quranic:root_000729:B001/m01`); removal of clothing (`quranic:root_000729:B002/m01`); following in another's track (`quranic:root_000175:B001/m01`); distant rebellious adversary (`quranic:root_000796:B004/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:175 `فَانْسَلَخَ`, `فَأَتْبَعَهُ`, and `الشَّيْطَانُ`
- Synthesis: Departure is an exposed state. The signs had functioned like an enclosing layer; shedding them leaves the person available to a pursuing force that immediately occupies the opened relation.

#### Subchannel B. Earth-Clinging Appetite That Keeps Panting
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Refusal of elevation becomes adherence to earth and desire, figured by a dog whose panting persists whether loaded against or left alone.
- Active motifs: clinging and settling (`quranic:root_000429:B002/m01`); heavy attachment to earth (`quranic:root_000025:B006/m01`); dog (`quranic:root_001312:B001/m01`); ravenous competition (`quranic:root_001312:B004/m01`); protruding tongue from thirst or strain (`quranic:root_001380:B001/m01`); heat of thirst (`quranic:root_001380:B002/m01`); imposed visible load (`quranic:root_000357:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:176 `أَخْلَدَ`, `الْأَرْضِ`, `هَوَاهُ`, `الْكَلْبِ`, `تَحْمِلْ`, and `يَلْهَثْ`
- Synthesis: The animal image diagnoses appetite by invariance: pressure does not create the panting, and release does not stop it. The condition is internally maintained, earthbound, and perpetually thirsty.

### 26. P10 (7:172-188) - Slow Entrapment and Fixed Time
- Semantic invariant: Delay can be an active mechanism that draws a subject step by step toward an endpoint whose time remains fixed and hidden.
- Surface relation: direct; 7:182-183 names gradual drawing, respite, and a firm plot; 7:185 and 7:187 name approaching term, fixed time, anchoring, heaviness, and sudden arrival.
- Surprising reach: Firmness includes ropes and tent cords, turning extended respite into a line that gives apparent room while remaining securely fastened.

#### Subchannel A. Respite as a Tightened Long Line
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A target is drawn by stages while time is extended; the extension remains part of a strong, controlled mechanism.
- Active motifs: taking by degrees (`quranic:root_000468:B003/m01`); plotted gradual leading (`quranic:root_001334:B002/m01`); temporal extension (`quranic:root_001446:B001/m01`); extended solidity (`quranic:root_001396:B001/m01`); tightening with cords (`quranic:root_001396:B008/m01`); granted head start in a race (`quranic:root_001396:B010/m01`)

- Synthesis: Delay is not absence of action. It lengthens the line on which the target moves, but the line remains taut, controlled, and attached to an unseen endpoint.

#### Subchannel B. The Anchored Hour Arrives Suddenly
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: An appointed term draws near; the hour has an anchorage and fixed time, bears cosmic weight, and arrives without warning.
- Active motifs: appointed endpoint (`quranic:root_000016:B001/m01`); temporal approach (`quranic:root_001212:B002/m01`); vessel brought to anchorage (`quranic:root_000564:B002/m01`); known time (`quranic:root_001671:B001/m01`); heaviness (`quranic:root_000202:B001/m01`); sudden surprise (`quranic:root_000135:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:185 `اقْتَرَبَ` and `أَجَلُهُمْ`; 7:187 `السَّاعَةِ`, `مُرْسَاهَا`, `لِوَقْتِهَا`, `ثَقُلَتْ`, and `بَغْتَةً`
- Synthesis: Hidden timing does not imply indeterminacy. The hour is fixed like an anchored object and heavy across the created order, yet its actual arrival ruptures prediction by coming suddenly.

### 27. P11 (7:189-206) - Reproductive Formation and Misassigned Agency
- Semantic invariant: Pairing produces a developing bodily load whose successful completion becomes the occasion for a false reassignment of creative agency.
- Surface relation: direct; 7:189-191 moves through one self, mate, intimacy, light and heavy pregnancy, birth request, partnership, and the contrast between creator and created.

- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A single self receives a mate, the pair enters intimate covering, and reproductive formation begins.
- Active motifs: marital mate (`quranic:root_000652:B002/m01`); joining one thing as another's pair (`quranic:root_000652:B003/m01`); intercourse under a covering expression (`quranic:root_001088:B004/m01`); identity and essence of the self (`quranic:root_001533:B012/m01`)
