#### Subchannel B. Load Grows, Then Agency Is Reassigned
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: An internal load begins light, becomes heavy, prompts a plea for sound offspring, and is followed by the assignment of partners.
- Active motifs: internal pregnancy or fruit (`quranic:root_000357:B002/m01`); lightness of a carried load (`quranic:root_000427:B001/m01`); heavy pregnancy (`quranic:root_000202:B007/m01`); childbirth and postpartum emergence (`quranic:root_001533:B005/m01`); claimed right or lineage (`quranic:root_000478:B002/m01`); shared partnership (`quranic:root_000791:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:189 `حَمَلَتْ`, `حَمْلًا`, `خَفِيفًا`, `أَثْقَلَتْ`, and `دَعَوَا`; 7:190 `شُرَكَاءَ`; 7:191 `يَخْلُقُ` and `يُخْلَقُونَ`
- Synthesis: Pregnancy is a changing load whose successful resolution exposes a question of agency. The pair calls during dependence, then converts the received outcome into a shared claim, even though the proposed partners are themselves made rather than makers.

### 28. P11 (7:189-206) - Embodied Responsiveness
- Semantic invariant: Genuine agency is disclosed through the ability to create, answer, perceive, remember, listen, and submit bodily.
- Surface relation: direct; 7:191-206 contrasts incapable objects with responsive protection, insight, recitation, remembrance, praise, and prostration.
- Surprising reach: The sequence forms a complete response circuit: disruptive touch is intercepted by remembrance, remembrance restores sight, hearing receives recitation, and the body ends in prostration.

#### Subchannel A. Agency That Cannot Answer or Aid
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Invoked objects neither create nor possess the capacity to aid, follow guidance, or answer a call.
- Active motifs: bringing creation into being (`quranic:root_000434:B002/m01`); capacity to act (`quranic:root_000956:B003/m01`); aid and support (`quranic:root_001510:B001/m01`); calling by voice (`quranic:root_000478:B001/m01`); verbal response (`quranic:root_000273:B003/m01`); cessation of sound (`quranic:root_000881:B001/m01`); direction toward a path (`quranic:root_001583:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:191 `يَخْلُقُ` and `يُخْلَقُونَ`; 7:192 and 7:197 `يَسْتَطِيعُونَ` and `نَصْرًا`; 7:193 `تَدْعُوهُمْ`, `الْهُدَى`, and `صَامِتُونَ`; 7:194 `ادْعُوهُمْ` and `فَلْيَسْتَجِيبُوا`
- Synthesis: Agency is tested as a chain of possible responses. The invoked object fails at every stage: it does not originate life, cannot support itself or another, does not follow direction, and cannot return a call.

#### Subchannel B. Anatomy Without Operation
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Legs, hands, eyes, and ears are named as possible instruments, but locomotion, grasp, sight, and hearing never occur.
- Active motifs: leg as bodily member (`quranic:root_000546:B001/m01`); voluntary walking (`quranic:root_001427:B001/m01`); bodily hand (`quranic:root_001693:B001/m01`); forceful grasp (`quranic:root_000126:B001/m01`); seeing eye (`quranic:root_001069:B001/m01`); visual perception (`quranic:root_000121:B001/m01`); bodily ear (`quranic:root_000022:B001/m01`); auditory perception (`quranic:root_000741:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:195 `أَرْجُلٌ`, `يَمْشُونَ`, `أَيْدٍ`, `يَبْطِشُونَ`, `أَعْيُنٌ`, `يُبْصِرُونَ`, `آذَانٌ`, and `يَسْمَعُونَ`; 7:198 `يَسْمَعُوا`, `يَنْظُرُونَ`, and `يُبْصِرُونَ`
- Synthesis: The critique separates component from function. Possessing the shape or name of an organ does not establish agency; an instrument counts only when it performs its operation within a responsive body.

#### Subchannel C. Intrusion Interrupted by Remembrance
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A corrupting impulse approaches, refuge is sought, a passing satanic touch occurs, remembrance activates, and insight returns.
- Active motifs: incitement that corrupts relations (`quranic:root_001490:B001/m01`); protective refuge (`quranic:root_001059:B001/m01`); passing apparition or intrusive touch (`quranic:root_000957:B003/m01`); recollection after lapse (`quranic:root_000516:B003/m01`); inward insight (`quranic:root_000121:B002/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:200 `يَنْزَغَنَّكَ`, `نَزْغٌ`, and `فَاسْتَعِذْ`; 7:201 `طَائِفٌ`, `تَذَكَّرُوا`, and `مُبْصِرُونَ`
- Synthesis: Protection is a responsive sequence rather than a static wall. Intrusion is noticed, refuge redirects the relation, remembrance reactivates what was latent, and perception becomes clear again.

#### Subchannel D. Recitation Received Through Attentive Silence
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Collected words are recited; listeners direct hearing toward them and suspend competing speech.
- Active motifs: reading and recitation (`quranic:root_001210:B002/m01`); understanding and compliance through hearing (`quranic:root_000741:B003/m01`); silence maintained for listening (`quranic:root_001508:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:204 `قُرِئَ`, `الْقُرْآنُ`, `فَاسْتَمِعُوا`, and `أَنْصِتُوا`
- Synthesis: Reception requires an arranged sensory field. Recitation gathers speech into a delivered form, hearing turns toward it, and attentive silence removes interference so that understanding can follow sound.

#### Subchannel E. Quiet Daily Remembrance Ends in Prostration
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Remembrance moves between inner and voiced speech at morning and evening, then becomes praise, worship, and bodily lowering.
- Active motifs: inward recollection (`quranic:root_000516:B003/m01`); raised public voice (`quranic:root_000269:B001/m01`); first part of the day (`quranic:root_001076:B001/m01`); evening after afternoon (`quranic:root_000038:B003/m01`); submissive worship (`quranic:root_000973:B003/m01`); praise and prayer (`quranic:root_000666:B001/m01`); bodily prostration (`quranic:root_000675:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:205 `اذْكُرْ`, `نَفْسِكَ`, `الْجَهْرِ`, `بِالْغُدُوِّ`, and `الْآصَالِ`; 7:206 `عِبَادَتِهِ`, `يُسَبِّحُونَهُ`, and `يَسْجُدُونَ`
- Synthesis: Responsiveness becomes rhythmic and embodied. Inner recollection is calibrated below loud speech across the day's two edges, then the whole body answers through worship, praise, and descent to the ground.

## Standalone Subchannels

### S1. P3 (7:40-58) - Celestial Covering and Ordered Motion
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Night covers day while sun, moon, and stars occupy a coordinated order.
- Active motifs: covering layer (`quranic:root_001088:B001/m01`); night darkness (`quranic:root_001392:B001/m01`); daylight opening (`quranic:root_001559:B002/m01`); sun and its light (`quranic:root_000818:B001/m01`); moon and its light (`quranic:root_001255:B001/m01`); rising star (`quranic:root_001475:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:54 `اللَّيْلَ`, `يُغْشِي`, `النَّهَارَ`, `الشَّمْسَ`, `الْقَمَرَ`, and `النُّجُومَ`
- Synthesis: The scene combines concealment and regulated recurrence. Night acts as a moving cover over daylight, while the named celestial bodies remain distinct participants in a coordinated temporal system.

### S2. P4 (7:59-72) - Ark Passage Through Overwhelming Water
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A vessel circles or rides within disturbed water while those outside it are submerged.
- Active motifs: ship moving on water (`quranic:root_001177:B003/m01`); agitated waves (`quranic:root_001177:B007/m01`); sinking to death (`quranic:root_001080:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:64 `الْفُلْكِ` and `أَغْرَقْنَا`
- Synthesis: The ark is defined by differential relation to the same water: it carries one group on the moving surface while the flood occupies and overwhelms the space of another.

### S3. P6 (7:103-129) - Patience Poured into a Mortal Vessel
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Patience is requested as a poured substance that fills and restrains the self until death.
- Active motifs: pouring and emptying a vessel (`quranic:root_001147:B002/m01`); restraining the self from panic (`quranic:root_000840:B001/m01`); confinement under threat of execution (`quranic:root_000840:B002/m01`); taking the soul at death (`quranic:root_001669:B002/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:126 `أَفْرِغْ`, `صَبْرًا`, and `تَوَفَّنَا`
- Synthesis: Patience is imagined as both content and containment. It must be poured into persons so they can hold themselves steady while coercive confinement and death remain immediately present.

### S4. P7 (7:130-147) - Inscription Gripped with Rope-Like Strength
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Broad tablets receive writing and decree, then must be taken with gathered strength.
- Active motifs: broad writing board (`quranic:root_001384:B003/m01`); written signs (`quranic:root_001283:B002/m01`); fixed decree (`quranic:root_001283:B003/m01`); strength gathered like rope strands (`quranic:root_001274:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:145 `الْأَلْوَاحِ`, `وَكَتَبْنَا`, and `بِقُوَّةٍ`
- Synthesis: Durable medium, inscription, obligation, and force form one handling scene. The text is fixed on a broad surface, but its practical continuity depends on a grip as gathered and tensile as a cord.

### S5. P9 (7:159-171) - Scattering, Testing, and Return
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A people is dispersed into separate directions, tested by contrasting conditions, and oriented toward return.
- Active motifs: scattering in many directions (`quranic:root_000153:B009/m01`); division into parts (`quranic:root_001240:B008/m01`); trial that exposes condition (`quranic:root_000153:B002/m01`); return to an earlier direction or state (`quranic:root_000544:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:168 `وَقَطَّعْنَاهُمْ`, `وَبَلَوْنَاهُمْ`, and `يَرْجِعُونَ`
- Synthesis: Dispersion does not end relation. Separate placement multiplies the sites of testing, while return remains the directional possibility toward which contrasting conditions press.

### S6. P10 (7:172-188) - Faculties Present but Unused
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Hearts, eyes, and ears remain anatomically present but fail to understand, see, or hear, reducing human capacity to unattended livestock.
- Active motifs: heart as organ of understanding (`quranic:root_001248:B001/m01`); comprehension (`quranic:root_001171:B001/m01`); seeing eye (`quranic:root_001069:B001/m01`); visual perception (`quranic:root_000121:B001/m01`); bodily ear (`quranic:root_000022:B001/m01`); auditory perception (`quranic:root_000741:B001/m01`); grazing livestock (`quranic:root_001525:B005/m01`); lapse of attention (`quranic:root_001097:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:179 `قُلُوبٌ`, `يَفْقَهُونَ`, `أَعْيُنٌ`, `يُبْصِرُونَ`, `آذَانٌ`, `يَسْمَعُونَ`, `الْأَنْعَامِ`, and `الْغَافِلُونَ`
- Synthesis: Incapacity is functional, not anatomical. Every component remains available, but no operation completes; heedlessness is the state in which an equipped perceptual system produces no guidance.

### S7. P10 (7:172-188) - Invocation Kept from Sideways Deviation
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Names direct invocation, while deviation bends naming and speech away from their proper referent.
- Active motifs: name as designation (`quranic:root_000745:B005/m01`); calling by speech (`quranic:root_000478:B001/m01`); leaning away from straightness (`quranic:root_001345:B001/m01`); verbal objection and dispute (`quranic:root_001345:B004/m01`); movement toward a side (`quranic:root_001345:B005/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:180 `الْأَسْمَاءُ`, `فَادْعُوهُ`, `يُلْحِدُونَ`, and `أَسْمَائِهِ`
- Synthesis: Naming establishes a verbal route to its referent. Deviation corrupts that route by leaning speech sideways, so invocation and misnaming become opposite operations on the same linguistic path.

### S8. P11 (7:189-206) - Low-Friction Social Handling
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: One takes the easy surplus, directs others toward recognized good, and turns aside from destabilizing ignorance.
- Active motifs: taking into one's handling (`quranic:root_000018:B001/m01`); easy surplus left without demand (`quranic:root_001032:B003/m01`); recognized good (`quranic:root_001002:B005/m01`); directive request (`quranic:root_000051:B002/m01`); turning one's side away (`quranic:root_001001:B005/m01`); agitated lack of judgment (`quranic:root_000271:B002/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:199 `خُذِ`, `الْعَفْوَ`, `وَأْمُرْ`, `بِالْعُرْفِ`, `وَأَعْرِضْ`, and `الْجَاهِلِينَ`
- Synthesis: The social protocol minimizes escalation through three coordinated operations: accept what comes without strain, actively maintain recognizable good, and deny destabilizing conduct the friction of reciprocal engagement.

### S9. Whole-surah - Bow Preparation, Full Draw, and Shot Outcome
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A bow is tested under tension; an arrow is feathered, notched, and set on the string; the archer draws fully and the shot either reaches, passes, or turns away from its target.
- Active motifs: bow bent close against its string under near-breaking tension (`quranic:root_000156:B005/m01`); testing a bow by pulling its string (`quranic:root_000526:B003/m01`); attaching feathers to an arrow (`quranic:root_000617:B003/m01`); cutting the arrow's nock (`quranic:root_001188:B009/m01`); setting the nock on the string (`quranic:root_001188:B009/m02`); drawing the bowstring (`quranic:root_001489:B002/m01`); reaching the furthest extent of the draw (`quranic:root_001080:B004/m01`); aiming and striking the target (`quranic:root_000889:B003/m01`); passing beyond the target (`quranic:root_000458:B018/m01`); swerving and falling elsewhere without a cut (`quranic:root_001464:B005/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:22 `ذَاقَا`; 7:26 `بَنِي` and `رِيشًا`; 7:27 `يَنزِعُ`; 7:41 `فَوْقِ`; 7:64 `أَغْرَقْنَا`; 7:72 `دَابِرَ`; 7:94 `نَبِيٍّ`; 7:100 `أَصَبْنَاهُم`
- Synthesis: This activation materializes the surah's repeated delivery of warning and exact consequence as a directed shot. Preparation, tension, and force do not by themselves constitute arrival: the decisive distinction is whether the projectile reaches, passes, or turns aside from its mark, usefully pressuring any reading that equates intensity with guidance.

### S10. Whole-surah - Opening and Clearing a Well
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A new shaft is excavated, may be abandoned before reaching water, and is entered and cleared until concealed water can gather within a bounded basin.
- Active motifs: newly excavated well (`quranic:root_000090:B008/m01`); unfinished well left before reaching water (`quranic:root_001244:B015/m01`); sides of a well or cistern (`quranic:root_001370:B004/m01`); descending into a well without being lowered (`quranic:root_000546:B013/m01`); removing water and mud until the water appears clear (`quranic:root_000269:B008/m01`); water collected in a basin (`quranic:root_001222:B002/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:16 `لَأَقْعُدَنَّ`; 7:29 `بَدَأَكُمْ`; 7:63 `رَجُلٍ`; 7:117 `تَلْقَفُ`; 7:161 `الْقَرْيَةَ`; 7:205 `الْجَهْرِ`
- Synthesis: The scene materializes the surah's water and disclosure readings as achieved access rather than spontaneous supply. An unfinished shaft stops short of contact, whereas descent and removal of obscuring mud make already present water visible and usable; revelation similarly requires an opening to be carried through and kept clear.

### S11. Whole-surah - Gaming Arrows Apportion a Slaughtered Camel
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Portions of a slaughtered camel are staked, marked gaming arrows are kept together and cast from the hand, and the resulting lot distinguishes awarded shares from loss.
- Active motifs: first share cut from a slaughtered camel (`quranic:root_000090:B006/m01`); divided cuts of the camel and gaming arrow (`quranic:root_001016:B009/m01`); leather receptacle holding the gaming arrows (`quranic:root_000532:B010/m01`); the named fifth gaming arrow (`quranic:root_001533:B016/m01`); casting the arrows from the hand (`quranic:root_001192:B004/m01`); gambling contest and victory over an opponent (`quranic:root_001255:B007/m01`); winning by depriving the opponent of what was sought (`quranic:root_000313:B007/m01`); losing arrow and stake lost in gambling (`quranic:root_000458:B019/m01`); completing the shares by feeding according to the winning arrow or taking the remainder (`quranic:root_000188:B006/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:3 `رَبِّكُمْ`; 7:9 `أَنفُسَهُمْ`; 7:29 `بَدَأَكُمْ`; 7:32 `حَرَّمَ`; 7:50 `أَفِيضُوا`; 7:54 `الْقَمَرَ`; 7:72 `دَابِرَ`; 7:137 `تَمَّتْ`; 7:142 `عَشْرٍ`
- Synthesis: This scene usefully pressures the surah's primary allocation and accountability reading by supplying a rival distribution mechanism. A cast can produce portions, winners, and losers, but it is not the surah's just scale or known water share; the activation clarifies that measured assignment is accountable order, not merely whatever allotment chance happens to deliver.

### S12. Whole-surah - Fire Assay, Slag, and Counterfeit Surface
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Metal emerges from a mine in unworked form, is tested by fire so slag separates from valued material, and can then be plated to display a precious surface over a different substance.
- Active motifs: mine or mineral source (`quranic:root_001475:B008/m01`); raw gold, silver, or mineral before shaping and striking (`quranic:root_000174:B002/m01`); testing gold or silver by fire to distinguish good from bad (`quranic:root_001128:B001/m01`); slag expelled by the bellows and exposed during smelting (`quranic:root_000386:B002/m01`); precious gold, silver, or metal vessel (`quranic:root_001077:B018/m01`); plating base metal with gold or silver so it appears otherwise (`quranic:root_001458:B005/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:27 `يَفْتِنَنَّكُمُ`; 7:50 `الْمَاءِ`; 7:54 `النُّجُومَ`; 7:58 `خَبُثَ`; 7:137 `مَغَارِبَهَا`; 7:139 `مُتَبَّرٌ`
- Synthesis: The assay supports the surah's primary reading of trial as discrimination: heat exposes composition and drives off slag. Plating then usefully pressures the calf's ornamented surface, because precious appearance can be manufactured without changing the underlying metal; visible brilliance is therefore not proof of purity, agency, or worth.

### S13. Whole-surah - Wagered Horse Race and Finishing Order
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Horses are matched on a course for a stake, riders release the reins for speed, and overtaking resolves the field into the horse ahead, the one immediately following, and the last arrival.
- Active motifs: a horse matching another in the run (`quranic:root_001335:B004/m01`); rider extending the reins to increase speed (`quranic:root_000151:B007/m01`); horse prancing vigorously in its run (`quranic:root_000138:B007/m01`); stake awarded to the winner of a race (`quranic:root_000671:B002/m01`); swift horse overtaking and leaving the field behind (`quranic:root_001240:B017/m01`); second horse following close behind the winner (`quranic:root_000879:B006/m01`); last horse in the racing field (`quranic:root_000724:B006/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:33 `الْبَغْيَ`; 7:62 `أُبَلِّغُكُمْ`; 7:72 `قَطَعْنَا`; 7:80 `سَبَقَكُمْ`; 7:85 `الْكَيْلَ`; 7:154 `سَكَتَ`; 7:170 `الصَّلَاةَ`
- Synthesis: The race reframes the surah's sequences, public contests, and assigned standings as course position resolved at a finish. Exertion and temporary proximity do not erase first, following, and last place; the attached stake makes final order consequential and supports the surah's distinction between motion before the term and standing when it arrives.

### S14. Whole-surah - Decoy, Hidden Hunter, and Set Snare
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A hunter enters a blind, erects a snare, and uses an owl decoy to draw a hawk downward while watching quietly for the bird to alight and become entangled.
- Active motifs: hunter entering a concealed blind (`quranic:root_000487:B001/m01`); erected hunting trap (`quranic:root_000879:B004/m01`); owl decoy prepared to draw down a hawk or falcon (`quranic:root_001384:B008/m01`); upward scouting gaze of hunter or hawk (`quranic:root_000256:B008/m01`); falcon or goshawk as quarry (`quranic:root_001040:B006/m01`); hunter's snare in which quarry becomes entangled (`quranic:root_000791:B006/m01`); hunter's faint whisper or rustle (`quranic:root_001651:B002/m01`); bird alighting on ground or tree (`quranic:root_001675:B006/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:7 `بِعِلْمٍ`; 7:20 `فَوَسْوَسَ`; 7:33 `تُشْرِكُوا`; 7:71 `وَقَعَ`; 7:137 `دَمَّرْنَا`; 7:143 `تَجَلَّى`; 7:145 `الْأَلْوَاحِ`; 7:170 `الصَّلَاةَ`
- Synthesis: This activation usefully pressures the surah's primary reading of signs and perception: a visible object can be planted to steer attention rather than guide it truthfully. The hidden arranger converts the quarry's look and descent into capture, materially extending the surah's scenes of unseen temptation, deceptive display, and gradual entrapment.

### S15. Whole-surah - Circumambulation Around an Erected Center
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A manufactured body or standing stone becomes a ritual center on which slaughter occurs and around which worshippers repeatedly circulate.
- Active motifs: worshipped body made from wood, silver, or copper (`quranic:root_000886:B001/m01`); stone erected for worship or slaughter (`quranic:root_001507:B002/m01`); blood poured over the standing stone (`quranic:root_001507:B002/m02`); idol, stone, or place serving as the center of circling (`quranic:root_000499:B006/m01`); repeated circumambulation around the center (`quranic:root_000957:B001/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:37 `نَصِيبُهُمْ`; 7:138 `أَصْنَامٍ`; 7:145 `دَارَ`; 7:201 `طَائِفٌ`
- Synthesis: The rite materializes the surah's critique of manufactured worship by placing all effective motion outside the object. The center receives form, blood, and human circulation but contributes no speech or guidance of its own, supporting the primary contrast between an intensely serviced idol and a responsive relation to divine address.

## Cross-Pericope Channels

### X1. P1 + P8 + P11 - Formation, Fabrication, and Assigned Agency
- Pericopes: P1 (7:1-25), P8 (7:148-158), and P11 (7:189-206)
- Bridge: contrast and role progression; the shared invariant is that visible bodily form does not by itself establish the source or powers of its maker.
- Canonical placements: P1 1A, "Form Estimated Before It Is Made"; P8 18A, "Ornament Assembled into a Body"; P11 27A, "Pairing and Concealed Intimacy"; P11 27B, "Load Grows, Then Agency Is Reassigned"
- Synthesis: P1 places estimation, material, and form within an originating creative act. P8 repeats bounded form as human fabrication but cannot supply living or guiding agency, while P11 carries generation through pregnancy and birth before exposing a false reassignment of authorship. The progression distinguishes creation, manufacture, and received reproduction rather than treating every formed body as evidence of equivalent agency.

### X2. P1 + P2 + P10 - Protective Layer, Removal, and Pursuit
- Pericopes: P1 (7:1-25), P2 (7:26-39), and P10 (7:172-188)
- Bridge: repeated scene signature and causal sequence; a covering protects a vulnerable interior, and removal or exit from that layer creates exposure to a following force.
- Canonical placements: P1 2B, "Concealment Breached and Patched"; P2 3A, "Clothing as Plumage and Armor"; P2 3B, "Stripping Exposes the Inside"; P10 25A, "Signs Shed Like Skin or Clothing"
- Synthesis: The first exposure prompts an improvised patch, the next pericope defines clothing as concealment and defense, and P10 transfers the same geometry to signs that are shed like skin. Pursuit begins at the opened boundary, so the bridge makes protective relation, not mere visual covering, the invariant across body, garment, and received sign.

### X3. P1 + P2 + P5 - Accountable Measure Versus Random Lot
- Pericopes: P1 (7:1-25), P2 (7:26-39), and P5 (7:73-102), with whole-surah lexical placement S11
- Bridge: shared invariant with contrast; legitimate allocation joins a measure, a due share, and an accountable recipient, while the gaming lot imitates distribution without preserving that order.
- Canonical placements: P1 1B, "Standing Made Heavy or Light"; P2 4B, "The Assigned Share Becomes a Taste"; P5 11B, "Exchange Calibrated Without Deficit"; S11, "Gaming Arrows Apportion a Slaughtered Camel"
- Synthesis: Weight first assigns standing, an allotted outcome then becomes experienced, and exchange protects another party's due through complete measure. The gaming-arrow scene reaches similar outputs of shares, winners, and losers through a cast. Its contrast clarifies that the surah's allocation is not validated by result alone but by calibrated and answerable assignment.

### X4. P3 + P7 + P9 - Released Water and Differentiated Outcome
- Pericopes: P3 (7:40-58), P7 (7:130-147), and P9 (7:159-171), with whole-surah lexical placement S10
- Bridge: repeated scene signature and reversal; a bounded source is opened or released into a receiving medium, and the resulting flow differentiates revival, passage, drowning, or regulated access.
- Canonical placements: P3 7A, "Cloud Load Delivered as Water"; P3 7B, "Land Sorts Water into Growth or Scarcity"; P7 15B, "Encompassing Water Sorts Passage from Drowning"; P9 21B, "Stone Opened into Known Water Shares"; S10, "Opening and Clearing a Well"
- Synthesis: Cloud, sea, stone, and well each hold water before a release operation changes access. Receiving land sorts growth, the sea reverses route into submersion, the struck stone divides one source into known shares, and well clearing makes concealed supply usable. Water is therefore a discriminating medium whose outcome depends on opening, receiver, and governed relation.

### X5. P4 + P8 + P9 + P11 - Address Carried, Fixed, Retained, and Heard
- Pericopes: P4 (7:59-72), P8 (7:148-158), P9 (7:159-171), and P11 (7:189-206)
- Bridge: role progression; the shared invariant is a communication chain that preserves address across carrier, durable medium, inherited handling, and attentive reception.
- Canonical placements: P4 8A, "A Message Carried to Its Limit"; P4 8B, "Counsel as Clean Repair"; P8 20A, "Instruction Fixed in a Durable Medium"; P9 23A, "Inherited Text Studied and Gripped"; P11 28D, "Recitation Received Through Attentive Silence"
- Synthesis: Delivery first requires a trustworthy carrier and intelligible arrival. Writing then stabilizes the address, inheritance and study maintain it across generations, and recitation returns fixed words to voiced transmission before hearing completes reception. The bridge is a role sequence, not a general theme of speech: each stage preserves what the next stage must receive.

### X6. P2 + P5 + P10 - Fixed Endpoint Through Delay and Surprise
- Pericopes: P2 (7:26-39), P5 (7:73-102), and P10 (7:172-188), with whole-surah lexical placement S13
- Bridge: causal sequence and contrast; an endpoint remains assigned even when approach is extended, hidden, or mistaken for ordinary time, and arrival resolves the apparent delay.
- Canonical placements: P2 5A, "A Term That Cannot Shift"; P2 5B, "Earlier and Later Parties Catch Up"; P5 12B, "Closure Arrives Off Schedule"; P10 26A, "Respite as a Tightened Long Line"; P10 26B, "The Anchored Hour Arrives Suddenly"; S13, "Wagered Horse Race and Finishing Order"
- Synthesis: P2 fixes the slot and preserves sequence, P5 shows closure interrupting expected schedules, and P10 makes respite an active line attached to an anchored hour. The race supplies the concrete resolution: movement before the finish may alter proximity but cannot abolish finishing order. Delay changes experience of approach, not the endpoint that assigns standing.

### X7. P1 + P5 + P10 + P11 - Four Relations to the Ground
- Pericopes: P1 (7:1-25), P5 (7:73-102), P10 (7:172-188), and P11 (7:189-206)
- Bridge: repeated embodied scene signature with contrast and reversal; a body is lowered, fixed, self-attached, or deliberately prostrated in relation to the same ground.
- Canonical placements: P1 2A, "Lowered Placement"; P5 10B, "Houses Become Sites of Immobilization"; P10 25B, "Earth-Clinging Appetite That Keeps Panting"; P11 28E, "Quiet Daily Remembrance Ends in Prostration"
- Synthesis: Imposed descent begins earthly settlement, catastrophe later fixes bodies to the ground, and appetite chooses an earthward attachment that no pressure changes. Final prostration reverses those relations by making bodily lowering a deliberate response rather than expulsion, defeat, or appetite. The repeated geometry gains meaning from agency and orientation.

### X8. P6 + P8 + P11 - Captured Perception Versus Guiding Agency
- Pericopes: P6 (7:103-129), P8 (7:148-158), and P11 (7:189-206), with whole-surah lexical placement S14
- Bridge: repeated signal test with contrast and reversal; perceptible display is judged by whether it merely captures attention or can guide, answer, and produce a responsive outcome.
- Canonical placements: P6 13B, "Sight Captured, Then the Display Swallowed"; P6 13C, "Defeat Becomes Bodily Inversion"; P8 18B, "Sound Without Speech or Direction"; P11 28A, "Agency That Cannot Answer or Aid"; P11 28B, "Anatomy Without Operation"; S14, "Decoy, Hidden Hunter, and Set Snare"
- Synthesis: Magic controls sight until a counter-sign removes the display and reverses allegiance. The calf's sound and the invoked bodies preserve perceptible form while failing speech, guidance, answer, and action; the decoy scene adds the sharper pressure that a visible signal can intentionally convert attention into capture. The invariant is completed agency, not sensory intensity.

### X9. P7 + P8 + P9 - Obligation as Tensile and Weight-Bearing Force
- Pericopes: P7 (7:130-147), P8 (7:148-158), and P9 (7:159-171), with pericope-local lexical placement S4
- Bridge: shared material invariant with reversal; obligation is handled as a maintained bond, tightened strand, carried restraint, firm grip, or overhead mass, while breach and release reverse those forces.
- Canonical placements: P7 16A, "Relief Conditioned by a Maintained Bond"; P7 16B, "The Tightened Bond Unravels"; P8 20B, "Yoke and Fetter Put Down"; P9 23B, "Mountain Lifted as Canopy and Constraint"; S4, "Inscription Gripped with Rope-Like Strength"
- Synthesis: Promise first behaves as a bond that can be maintained or pulled apart. Written obligation then acquires the weight of yoke and fetter, while firm gripping gathers strength like rope and the lifted mountain turns covenant into overhead load. Breach, release, grip, and constraint are opposite operations on one tensile and weight-bearing model of obligation.

## Whole-Surah Standalone Subchannels

### S16. Whole-surah - Hide Made into a Water-Holding Skin
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A stiff raw hide is opened and skinned, cleared of adhering flesh, tanned, cut, and sewn into a waterskin whose seams are conditioned and whose weak places are tested before filling.
- Active motifs: raw untanned hide (`quranic:root_000313:B002/m01`); hide opened for skinning (`quranic:root_000789:B006/m01`); flesh or fat left on the hide (`quranic:root_001102:B012/m01`); tanning leaves or bark (`quranic:root_000737:B008/m01`); leather cut for repair and waterskin manufacture (`quranic:root_001150:B001/m01`); close stitching of a skin (`quranic:root_000865:B004/m01`); leather thong joining the edges (`quranic:root_001312:B006/m01`); clay and water conditioning that seals the stitches (`quranic:root_000783:B013/m01`); thin place from which water leaks (`quranic:root_001069:B007/m01`); waterskin filled with water (`quranic:root_001431:B009/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:32 `حَرَّمَ`; 7:163 `شُرَّعًا`; 7:43 `غِلٍّ`; 7:46 `سَلَامٌ`; 7:37 `افْتَرَى`; 7:13 `صَاغِرِينَ`; 7:176 `كَلْبِ`; 7:31 `اشْرَبُوا`; 7:116 `أَعْيُنَ`; 7:84 `أَمْطَرْنَا`
- Synthesis: The scene materializes both the surah's protective covering and its governed water access. A skin becomes useful not by surface appearance but through removal, treatment, joined edges, and sealed apertures; one weak place defeats the container's relation to what it must preserve. It therefore supports the primary contrast between an outward form and a form made fit to carry provision.

### S17. Whole-surah - Sounding a Well and Raising a Balanced Bucket
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A weighted stone sounds the well's depth, an added rope section reaches the water, and a handled bucket is balanced, filled, raised, and made available for drinking.
- Active motifs: stone dropped or tied in a well to gauge depth by sound (`quranic:root_000543:B006/m01`); rope section joined to extend the drawline (`quranic:root_000471:B003/m01`); large bucket filled nearly or fully (`quranic:root_000521:B007/m01`); elongated bucket with one handle (`quranic:root_000737:B011/m01`); handle, side, or crosspiece balancing the bucket's load (`quranic:root_000741:B008/m01`); drinking directly from a full bucket (`quranic:root_001274:B005/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:71 `رِجْسٌ`; 7:38 `ادَّارَكُوا`; 7:100 `ذُنُوبِ`; 7:46 `سَلَامٌ`; 7:100 `يَسْمَعُوا`; 7:145 `بِقُوَّةٍ`
- Synthesis: This operation usefully extends S10 without duplicating excavation: the issue here is measurement and retrieval after a shaft exists. Hidden depth is inferred through a returned sound, then connected line and balanced container convert remote water into a drinkable share. The scene supports the surah's primary joining of signs, attentive hearing, measured access, and life-giving water.

### S18. Whole-surah - Timed Milking and Butter Separation
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Milk collected overnight is drawn from a kneeling camel, a small remainder is retained to call forth the next flow, and repeated milkings lead through thickening and churning to separated butter.
- Active motifs: morning milk drawn from a kneeling camel after overnight collection (`quranic:root_000109:B007/m01`); milk left in the udder to summon what follows (`quranic:root_000478:B003/m01`); milk returning during the interval between milkings (`quranic:root_001188:B006/m01`); abundant successive flow of milk (`quranic:root_000563:B006/m01`); butter gathering in milk or a churned skin (`quranic:root_000205:B004/m01`); clarified fat separated from butter and milk (`quranic:root_000430:B008/m01`); milk thickening or curdling at its later stage (`quranic:root_000067:B005/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:54 `تَبَارَكَ`; 7:5 `دَعْوَاهُمْ`; 7:41 `فَوْقِهِمْ`; 7:6 `أُرْسِلَ`; 7:57 `الثَّمَرَاتِ`; 7:29 `مُخْلِصِينَ`; 7:38 `أُولَاهُمْ`
- Synthesis: Provision here is neither instantaneous nor exhausted in one taking. Retention, interval, renewed flow, and separation produce the valued outcome, materializing the surah's primary readings of measured shares, appointed timing, and productive differentiation. The scene especially pressures extraction without restraint: stripping the source completely would interrupt the sequence that yields more.

### S19. Whole-surah - A Foster Calf Accepted through a Simulated Birth
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: After a camel loses her young, a wrapped insert is used to simulate parturition so that she accepts another calf, lets it nurse, and eventually releases it into weaning.
- Active motifs: bereaved camel distressed by the loss of her calf (`quranic:root_000987:B006/m01`); calf-less camel induced to accept and milk for another young (`quranic:root_000436:B010/m01`); wrapped cloth inserted to simulate birth for foster nursing (`quranic:root_000468:B007/m01`); calf released with the mother to suckle at will (`quranic:root_000546:B014/m01`); young animal separated from its mother or milk at weaning (`quranic:root_001159:B003/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:148 `عِجْلًا`; 7:38 `خَلَتْ`; 7:182 `سَنَسْتَدْرِجُهُمْ`; 7:46 `رِجَالٌ`; 7:32 `نُفَصِّلُ`
- Synthesis: A fabricated bodily cue can trigger a real caregiving response without establishing true birth or genealogy. That mechanism usefully pressures the surah's calf and deceptive-display readings: an effective sensory trigger is not proof of the object's origin, authorship, or rightful authority. The living relation belongs to the responsive mother and dependent calf, not to the simulated sign that redirects recognition.

### S20. Whole-surah - Banked Embers Stirred into Transforming Fire
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Fuel and embers are buried so fire survives in a quiet state, then stirred back into ignition until heat takes meat and changes its substance.
- Active motifs: fire banked in earth with fuel so it remains (`quranic:root_001424:B008/m01`); embers stirred until they ignite (`quranic:root_001639:B005/m01`); meat taken by fire until its liquid runs and it changes (`quranic:root_001266:B002/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:170 `يُمَسِّكُونَ`; 7:43 `أُورِثْتُمُوهَا`; 7:127 `قَاهِرُونَ`
- Synthesis: The scene reframes apparent quiet as retained capacity rather than absence. Banking, reactivation, and irreversible change form a compact causal sequence that supports the surah's primary treatment of respite and sudden closure: a force can remain held through an interval and still arrive with material consequence once activated.

### S21. Whole-surah - A Wound Opened, Drained, and Tested by Relapse
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A wound swells and gathers pus, is opened and treated with medicine and stitching, then reveals whether repair was complete by scarring cleanly or reopening over concealed corruption.
- Active motifs: wound swelling and advancing toward corruption (`quranic:root_000138:B004/m01`); pus collected in an abscess or wound (`quranic:root_000281:B006/m01`); incision made to open a wound (`quranic:root_001638:B002/m01`); physician treating and sewing the wound (`quranic:root_000034:B001/m01`); healed skin retaining a scar or relapsing (`quranic:root_000289:B004/m01`); wound closed over corruption and breaking open again (`quranic:root_001071:B003/m01`); disease or wound worsening after improvement (`quranic:root_001096:B004/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:33 `الْبَغْيَ`; 7:4 `جَاءَهَا`; 7:70 `وَنَذَرَ`; 7:93 `آسَى`; 7:147 `حَبِطَتْ`; 7:83 `الْغَابِرِينَ`; 7:23 `تَغْفِرْ`
- Synthesis: This medical sequence materially sharpens the surah's repeated affliction, relief, reform, and relapse pattern. Surface closure is not healing when corruption remains underneath; repair requires exposure, removal, and a join that holds after pressure returns. It therefore usefully pressures temporary relief followed by renewed breach as an unhealed condition rather than a completed restoration.

### S22. Whole-surah - Burial in a Lateral Chamber
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: The grave becomes a second house: the body is covered, placed on its right side in a lateral niche, and enclosed when earth is heaped over the opening.
- Active motifs: grave named as the dead person's house (`quranic:root_000166:B007/m01`); corpse concealed with grave covering or shroud (`quranic:root_000266:B009/m01`); earth heaped over the dead in burial (`quranic:root_000482:B003/m01`); side chamber cut in the grave for the body (`quranic:root_001345:B002/m01`); dead person laid on the right side (`quranic:root_001698:B007/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:4 `بَيَاتًا`; 7:19 `الْجَنَّةَ`; 7:143 `دَكًّا`; 7:180 `يُلْحِدُونَ`; 7:17 `أَيْمَانِهِمْ`
- Synthesis: Interment materializes the surah's return-to-earth reading as a deliberate sequence of placement and concealment. Calling the grave a house also intensifies P5's reversal from inhabited shelter to bodily stillness. Against these closing operations, the primary promise of being brought forth from earth is an exact reversal: enclosure opens and the placed body exits its second dwelling.

### S23. Whole-surah - Drum, Lute, Refrain, and Listening
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A one-faced drum and a struck wooden instrument accompany raised song; the voice returns in refrain and listeners receive it as pleasurable sound.
- Active motifs: one-faced drum (`quranic:root_001281:B012/m01`); wooden oud or mizhar used as an instrument (`quranic:root_001058:B010/m01`); singing voice and song (`quranic:root_001110:B003/m01`); repeated or ornamented return of the voice in song or recitation (`quranic:root_000544:B007/m01`); pleasing sound received in listening (`quranic:root_000741:B007/m01`); raised riding-song or chant (`quranic:root_001507:B009/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:13 `تَتَكَبَّرَ`; 7:29 `تَعُودُونَ`; 7:48 `أَغْنَى`; 7:150 `رَجَعَ`; 7:100 `يَسْمَعُونَ`; 7:37 `نَصِيبُهُمْ`
- Synthesis: The performance completes an auditory scene in which rhythm, repetition, and pleasure can hold attention without supplying direction. It usefully pressures the surah's distinction between the calf's sound and guiding speech, while also clarifying why attentive silence before recitation is not mere acoustic reception: patterned sound becomes guidance only when intelligible address and responsive agency accompany it.

### S24. Whole-surah - Incense Ground, Stored, Applied, and Detected
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Aromatic woods and medicinal incense are ground on a stone, reduced to powder or paste, stored with the perfumer's tools, applied, and recognized through the scent they release.
- Active motifs: aloe wood burned as incense (`quranic:root_000076:B014/m01`); qist wood used in incense or medicine (`quranic:root_001224:B006/m01`); broad stone for grinding perfume (`quranic:root_000879:B008/m01`); powdered aromatic substance (`quranic:root_000511:B003/m01`); scented paste applied as a coating (`quranic:root_000434:B010/m01`); box holding perfume and its tools (`quranic:root_000468:B006/m01`); scent acquired and perceived by smell (`quranic:root_000609:B004/m01`); fragrance used to scent or identify what bears it (`quranic:root_001002:B004/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: unavailable for root `ء ل ي`; 7:29 `بِالْقِسْطِ`; 7:170 `الصَّلَاةَ`; 7:172 `ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ`; 7:11 `خَلَقْنَاكُمْ`; 7:182 `سَنَسْتَدْرِجُهُمْ`; 7:57 `الرِّيَاحَ`; 7:46 `الْأَعْرَافِ`
- Synthesis: Fragrance supplies a complete counter-model to purely visual evidence: an unseen substance becomes knowable through a distributed but specific effect on its receiver. Grinding and application make the trace, storage preserves its source, and smell recognizes its presence. The scene reframes the surah's signs and perception by showing that reliable manifestation need not resemble a visible body or spectacle.

### S25. Whole-surah - Consecration, Pilgrim Flow, and Appointed Sacrifice
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Worshippers enter consecration, stand at Arafat, depart together, and lead a marked sacrificial animal to its appointed sanctuary before slaughter and preservation of its meat.
- Active motifs: entering the consecrated state for pilgrimage (`quranic:root_000313:B004/m01`); standing at Arafat (`quranic:root_001002:B007/m01`); collective departure from Arafat like a released flow (`quranic:root_001192:B002/m01`); sacrificial animal or offering sent to the sanctuary (`quranic:root_001583:B005/m01`); animal marked by blood as a ritual sign (`quranic:root_000798:B006/m01`); offering reaching its appointed place (`quranic:root_000351:B004/m01`); sacrifice made on the festival day (`quranic:root_000904:B004/m01`); sacrificial meat exposed to sun and dried during the following days (`quranic:root_000790:B002/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:32 `حَرَّمَ`; 7:46 `الْأَعْرَافِ`; 7:50 `أَفِيضُوا`; 7:30 `هَدَى`; 7:95 `يَشْعُرُونَ`; 7:157 `يُحِلُّ`; 7:98 `ضُحًى`; 7:137 `مَشَارِقَ`
- Synthesis: This rite is a role-and-sequence structure rather than a generic worship domain: consecrated participant, fixed station, communal movement, marked offering, appointed endpoint, and completed act. It supports the surah's primary distinction between responsive worship and manufactured sacred objects. Meaning resides in received order and accountable action, not in servicing an inert center.

### S26. Whole-surah - Cloth Completed, Cut, Padded, and Dyed
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Additional wool completes a strong weave, the cloth is cut and first-seamed, cotton is quilted into it, and dye gives the finished garment a surface that may either disclose or exaggerate its quality.
- Active motifs: extra wool sought to finish an incomplete weaving (`quranic:root_000188:B007/m01`); cloth strong through abundant yarn (`quranic:root_000043:B012/m01`); well-made weave and twist (`quranic:root_000217:B007/m01`); first seam made before finishing (`quranic:root_001445:B009/m01`); cloth cut and tailored into a garment (`quranic:root_001240:B012/m01`); cotton laid and sewn into a padded coat (`quranic:root_001657:B008/m01`); cloth saturated with saffron-red or yellow dye (`quranic:root_000245:B003/m01`); multicolored cloth whose appearance misstates its condition (`quranic:root_001290:B009/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:137 `تَمَّتْ`; 7:19 `كُلَا`; 7:74 `الْجِبَالَ`; 7:88 `مِلَّتِنَا`; 7:72 `قَطَعْنَا`; 7:157 `يَضَعُ`; 7:148 `جَسَدًا`; 7:36 `كَذَّبُوا`
- Synthesis: The craft scene materializes the surah's clothing and adornment reading through internal construction: completion, weave, cut, seam, and padding produce protection, while dye produces visible finish. The deceptive-cloth motif usefully pressures appearance by separating color from structural quality. A garment can look complete while its true strength still lies in hidden joins and material density.

### S27. Whole-surah - Padding a Camel for Rider and Load
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A camel is fitted with belly girth, back pad, and leather saddle covering, lowers its neck so a rider can mount, and bears on its skin the sore when the load-bearing arrangement fails.
- Active motifs: girth fastened beneath the camel's belly (`quranic:root_000128:B006/m01`); pad or saddlecloth placed around the hump (`quranic:root_000766:B010/m01`); leather covering over the saddle (`quranic:root_001128:B008/m01`); camel lowering its neck to receive the rider's foot (`quranic:root_001657:B013/m01`); saddle sore and riding abrasion left on the back (`quranic:root_001675:B010/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:33 `بَطَنَ`; 7:54 `اسْتَوَى`; 7:27 `يَفْتِنَنَّكُمُ`; 7:157 `يَضَعُ`; 7:71 `وَقَعَ`
- Synthesis: The scene materializes burden as an engineered bodily relation. Girth and padding distribute force, voluntary lowering permits the rider's ascent, and a sore records failed mediation between body and load. It supports the surah's primary handling of yokes, carried obligations, and prostration by distinguishing a load responsibly fitted from one whose pressure simply wounds its bearer.

### S28. Whole-surah - Amulet, Binding Charm, and Assigned Protection
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Fear of an injuring gaze leads to incantations, knots, and beads hung on a person or child and credited with restraining another, turning a heart, or blocking harm.
- Active motifs: injuring gaze or evil eye (`quranic:root_001533:B003/m01`); charm or bead claimed to seize the eye and restrain a person (`quranic:root_000018:B004/m01`); amulet hung on a child for supposed protection (`quranic:root_000188:B002/m01`); bead claimed to turn a person's heart (`quranic:root_000860:B009/m01`); incantation or amulet used against fear, madness, eye, or illness (`quranic:root_001059:B002/m01`); magical knot and its undoing (`quranic:root_001036:B014/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:9 `أَنْفُسَهُمْ`; 7:30 `اتَّخَذُوا`; 7:137 `تَمَّتْ`; 7:47 `صُرِفَتْ`; 7:200 `فَاسْتَعِذْ`; 7:169 `يَعْقِلُونَ`
- Synthesis: The practice assigns invisible causal power to manufactured objects and performed bindings, making it a compact pressure test for the surah's magic, idol, and agency readings. A bead can be worn and a knot manipulated, but the claimed protection or control is an attribution layered onto the object. The scene strengthens the primary move from deceptive capture toward refuge in an answering source of aid.

### S29. Whole-surah - Star Reader and Claimed Hidden Knowledge
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A star reader studies visible celestial paths and presents the observation as access to hidden information for those who consult a diviner or astrologer.
- Active motifs: celestial sphere and courses of stars (`quranic:root_001177:B002/m01`); observing stars as an astrological practice (`quranic:root_001475:B005/m01`); diviner, astrologer, or soothsayer claiming hidden knowledge (`quranic:root_001002:B012/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:64 `الْفُلْكِ`; 7:54 `النُّجُومُ`; 7:46 `الْأَعْرَافِ`
- Synthesis: The scene directly pressures the surah's primary treatment of the Hour in 7:187. Regular visible motion can support observation, but it does not authorize a claim to the concealed time of arrival. The lexical activation therefore separates reading signs from possessing the unseen: a patterned sky is not a transferred key to the fixed endpoint.

### S30. Whole-surah - Earth Wiped onto the Limbs of Prayer
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Clean earth is deliberately sought and wiped across face and hands in preparation for prayer, after which the same embodied surface and limbs enter prostration.
- Active motifs: ritual use of clean earth to wipe face and hands for prayer (`quranic:root_001697:B002/m01`); face as the body's presented surface (`quranic:root_001630:B001/m01`); forehead, hands, knees, and feet as limbs of prostration (`quranic:root_000675:B003/m01`)
- Ayah anchors: 7:136 `الْيَمِّ`; 7:29 `وُجُوهَكُمْ`; 7:11 `اسْجُدُوا`
- Synthesis: This rite reframes the surah's earthward bodily geometry. Earth is neither merely the site of expulsion nor the object of appetite; under a directed operation it becomes a medium of readiness, and the prepared body answers by lowering itself. The scene thus supports the primary distinction between involuntary abasement, earth-clinging desire, and deliberate worship.
